# Automatic table border colors

Original OOXML controls generated by `tools/automatic_table_borders_fixture.py`.
No third-party document or font binaries are included. The package scaffold is
the project's original exhausted-cell-indents fixture.

Each document has eight 2-by-2 tables over two pages: table-level and cell-level
automatic borders on black, dark blue, light gray and alternating black/white
cell fills. Both outer and internal edges are exercised. The second document
adds a dark blue page background. The reference application exported
the retained PDFs after opening and verifying each source path.

The reference application paints every automatic border black, regardless of those backgrounds.
`tools/automatic_table_borders_reference.py` extracts native RGB samples and
records source/PDF SHA-256 hashes. Browser tests check color, editable opening,
unchanged package parts, retained automatic declarations, exact undo and reopening.
The unit controls also retain contrasting automatic text/paragraph ink and
explicit RGB border colors.

Known separate gap: outer T-junctions have small raster seams in the browser.
Ten of the original 200 samples per white-page document differed by 1–51 RGB
levels there. Replacing only automatic colors with explicit black produces
identical complete browser page rasters on both light and dark pages, confirming
this is independent of automatic color resolution. The color samples exclude
outer T-junctions; existing corner/crossing geometry regressions remain enabled.
This fixture does not claim pixel-perfect border junction geometry.

ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §17.3.4 permits the consumer to select automatic
border colors; §§17.4.38 and 17.4.66 define table/cell border application and
conflicts. The reference application's black choice is verified behavior, not a proven normative
contradiction. The source retains `auto`; color resolution occurs in painting
and border conflict comparison, without changing serialization or text colors.
